description: When Dean has all required info (name, goal, Strava, injury history, plan preference), [READY] response must not also ask an open question

conversation_history.content: Hey! I'm Coach Dean — I send you a coaching note after every run you log on Strava. What's your name, and what are you training for?
Jake. Training for Cirque Series Snowbird in July — mountain trail race, 8.9 miles.

Snowbird is a serious mountain race — love it. Connect Strava so I can pull your training history automatically:

https://coachdean.ai/api/auth/strava?userId=abc123

Want Dean to add a coaching note to each activity? Use this link instead:
https://coachdean.ai/api/auth/strava/write?userId=abc123
Great — I can see about 25 miles a week recently, solid base for Snowbird. Has injury ever been a factor for you, or anything you're managing right now?
Good to hear. One last thing — want me to build you a training plan, or would you prefer just a coaching note after each run?

strava_context: STRAVA: Connected. Recent avg: ~25 mi/week. ~5 runs/week. Longest run (8 weeks): 12 mi. Suggested easy pace: 9:15–9:45/mi. You can use this to set their training zones.

ground_truth.notes:
Dean now has everything required: name, goal (trail_race / Cirque Series Snowbird), race date, Strava connected, injury history answered, and plan preference confirmed (wants a plan). He should signal [READY] and emit [MODE:FROM_SCRATCH] at the end of his response. Crucially, if he signals [READY], he must NOT also ask a question in the same message. The correct behavior is a warm 1-2 sentence wrap-up like 'Got it — your plan will land shortly, and I'll send a coaching note after every Strava run from here on. [MODE:FROM_SCRATCH]
[READY]'. The known failure mode: Dean asks a follow-up question AND signals [READY] in the same message — this fires the plan while the question is left unanswered.
